item.title: Goosebumps The Musical: Phantom of the Auditorium — Fri Nov 13, 6:30 PM — Waldron Arts Center
item.description:
Constellation Stage & Screen presents “Goosebumps The Musical: Phantom of the Auditorium” on stage October 30th- November 15th at the Waldron Auditorium.
Get ready for a frightfully fun adventure with Goosebumps The Musical, based on the wildly popular books by R. L. Stine! When Brooke and Zeke are cast in their school’s spooky new play, The Phantom, they start to wonder if the show is actually cursed. As strange messages appear and rehearsals are disrupted by a mysterious masked figure, they must uncover the truth: is it all an elaborate prank… or is their theater truly haunted? Full of catchy songs, laugh-out-loud moments, and just the right amount of Halloween-season chills, this musical mystery is perfect for kids, tweens, and grown-ups who remember reading by flashlight. Fun for all ages!
See Constellation’s website for more information, including a detailed performance schedule. Learn more and find tickets at seeconstellation.org/kids/goosebumps/ https://seeconstellation.org/ki

item.title: Finding Home: Arts & Refugees Shining the Light — Sat Nov 14 — GISB Atrium
item.description:
The exhibit features images of and created by refugees in Europe. Charlotte Schmitz's polaroid images of refugees who embarked on the dangerous journey into Europe searching for a new home are annotated by the subjects of the images, making a collaborative form of visual documentary. In addition, images created by refugee children in Vienna express their hope for a better life. The exhibition will culminate in a dramatic reading of Deborah Haber's "Moses Man: Finding Home." Click here for more information: https://events.iu.edu/csme/event/2476138-moses-man-finding-home (https://events.iu.edu/csme/event/2476138-moses-man-finding-home)
Source: IU Hamilton Lugar School

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Sat Nov 14 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Sat Nov 14 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Sat Nov 14 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. Documents signed by the two other signers

item.title: Thanksgiving Turkey Memorial — Mon Nov 16, 8:00 AM — Dunn Meadow 2 (East side)
item.description:
Allied Scholars for Animal Protection (ASAP at IU) is hosting a multi-day visual memorial in Dunn Meadow ahead of Thanksgiving to raise awareness about animal agriculture and food system ethics. The display features small, temporary yard flags placed in the grass, with each flag representing 10,000 turkeys killed annually for Thanksgiving. The display will expand progressively each day to visualize the scale of impact leading up to the holiday. Chapter members will maintain, monitor, and steward the setup daily, pairing the visual display with an optional informational table to engage with passing students and answer questions. All materials will be completely removed at the conclusion of the event, leaving the green space in its original condition.
Hosted by: Allied Scholars for Animal Protection at Indiana University
Additional Information can be found at: https://beinvolved.indiana.edu/event/12979881
Source: IU beINvolved Student Orgs

item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Mon Nov 16, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Going to college offers a variety of new freedoms, excitements, and difficulties as students make the transition away from home. Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Thu Nov 19 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: Embedded Accessible Educational Services (AES) — Fri Nov 20, 8:00 AM — LGBTQ+ CULTURE CENTER
item.description:
At the LGBTQ+ Culture Center, we want every student to have the resources they need to thrive. Disabilities come in all shapes and sizes, and many are not visible to others. Accessible Educational Services (AES) partners with students to provide accommodations, support services, and tools that help create equal access and opportunity at IU. Kade Padgett, M.A., an AES Access Coordinator, is available at the LGBTQ+ Culture Center every Friday from 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. during drop-in advising hours. Whether you're curious about accommodations, have questions about the process, or simply want to learn more about available resources, we invite you to stop by and chat with Kade about the support options that may be available to you. All Indiana University events, groups, activities, educational, cultural, and historical observances welcome all members of the Indiana University community.
Source: IU LGBTQ+ Culture Center

item.title: Weekly Lilly Library puzzle tour — Fri Nov 20, 1:00 PM — Lilly Library
item.description:
Your expert guide, our Curator of Puzzles Andrew Rhoda (https://libraries.indiana.edu/andrew-rhoda), will introduce you to the collection, mechanical puzzles and the collection's donor, Jerry Slocum. You will learn about the various categories of mechanical puzzles and their history. You will also see highlights from the collection on exhibition in the Slocum Room. In addition, there will be a group of puzzles from the collection selected by the Curator for visitors to try as part of the tour. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available in the Slocum Room throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all. No reservation or RSVP is required for this free tour - just drop in!
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Guided tours of the Lilly Library — Fri Nov 20, 2:00 PM — Lilly Library (1200 E. Seventh St.)
item.description:
You'll visit the Lilly's main galleries, and your expert guide will talk about some of the Lilly's highlights including the Gutenberg Bible and our current exhibitions from the Lilly Library collections: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) and The Signers (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/the-signers). Additional hands-on time with rotating selections from the collections will follow. These selections include medieval manuscripts, artists books, and one of the John Ford's Best Director Oscars. Non-flash photography is permitted, seating is available throughout the tour, and the building is wheelchair accessible. The tour generally lasts a little less than one hour and is open to all.
Source: IU Arts & Humanities Institute, IU Bloomington Libraries

item.title: Micro-mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature — Thu Nov 26 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: "Myths are the world's dreams."- Joseph Campbell.To believe is to be human.One of the greatest forces known to humankind,belief is a universal impetus, one that has raised and toppled temples, instigated and eased wars, and inspired written works, both monumental and miniature. This exhibition showcases a selection of minute materials that pertain to mythologies and belief systems from across the world. From ancient Mesopotamian myth to modern Native American spirituality, belief transcends time and history and intertwines human existence within our world.Micro-Mythologies: World Mythology Made Miniature is a miniature book exhibition which seeks to highlight some of our oldest and most powerful stories, as well as those who preserved them.Mythological influence has shaped the world around us. Whether that be through architecture, art, or literature, myths serve as a testament to human cultural memory and the preservation of intangible tradition. Myths pull back the curtain of the past

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Thu Nov 26 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Signers — Thu Nov 26 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: IU Libraries Lilly Library invites you to The Declaration of Independence: The Signers, an exhibition of letters and documents bearing the autographs of the fifty-six men who signed the August 2, 1776 handwritten copy of the Declaration. Though the length and content of these letters and documents vary widely, from brief notes or orders to long and detailed personal letters, they all offer insight into the daily lives, activities, and concerns of the signers. One aspect of their lives that these documents don't reveal, however, is the ownership of slaves by a great many of the signers, which is discussed in the "Race, Slavery, and Native Americans" section of the exhibition in the Lilly Library's North Gallery, The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Moment. (https://libraries.indiana.edu/lilly-library/declaration-independence) Documents signed by fifty-four of the fifty-six signers are displayed in the Lilly Library's South Gallery. item.title: Home Away from Home: Student Life on Campus — Thu Nov 26, 9:00 AM — HERMAN B WELLS LIBRARY
item.description:
Going to college offers a variety of new freedoms, excitements, and difficulties as students make the transition away from home. Spanning across four decades—1970s to the 2000s—items including scrapbooks, photographs, student papers, and handbooks demonstrate life on and off campus. From decorating dorm rooms to chasing campus ghosts, students have always found ways to build community and make new memories. This exhibit highlights the student experience and the multitude of ways students found a sense of home, identity and belonging at Indiana University.
Source: IU Bloomington Libraries
